case: The record's own declared example (sec 3.5 (1): caustic viscosity, domain T 293.15-333.15 K, w[NaOH] 0-0.30) in the triple-effect NaOH evaporator DEV.md 4c C377 decided (a), first effect near 130 C, and the 50 wt % duty of C377 (b); the solution record NaOH-water (Olsson et al. 1997, 0-200 C) present
what_the_rule_does: Methods are resolved at assembly; a declared correlation is tier 2a and 'outside [its domain], an announced extrapolation' (sec 3.5 (1)).  So effect 1 (and every state above 0.30) gets the plant fit extrapolated 70 K, although the catalogue law is inside ITS domain there.  Amendment 2 prints both values and counts a finding (deviation > 0.23 %), and the extrapolated value is still the one used, pinned and drawn
why_wrong_or_fine: WRONG.  The decline rests on respecting a DELIBERATE choice; the user's own declaration says the fit holds at 20-60 C and w <= 0.30, so using it at 130 C or w 0.5 is a choice the user did not make.  This is a concrete case where the order picks badly WITH the deviation printed.  Fine inside the declared domain: there the decline is right
proposed_wording: 'A case-declared correlation outranks a catalogue method only INSIDE the domain it declares.  Outside it, when a catalogue method applicable at that state exists, the request REFUSES naming both (the case widens its domain deliberately, or removes the correlation); it extrapolates, announced, only when no other method applies.'  (A refusal at the boundary introduces no hidden discontinuity: the run stops.)

point: (a) precedence; scope of a declared correlation
case: Same evaporator: the steam-chest condensate and any distillate are pure water; or any case with a caustic line and an ethanol stream
what_the_rule_does: sec 3.5 (1): 'Its property and phase are the block it is written in (no field)' -- a declared correlation carries NO constituent set, while a measurement names `system ( NaOH water )`.  At w[NaOH] = 0 the condensate is inside the declared domain, so the caustic fit replaces the water reference for it; an ethanol-water stream (w[NaOH] = 0) gets the caustic formula, ethanol ignored
why_wrong_or_fine: WRONG.  The precedence is decided per (property, phase, stream) but the method's applicability has no constituent test at all, so tier 2a captures phases the author never meant.  Amendment 2 prints a deviation for the condensate (counted, against IAPWS), but for the ethanol stream the beaten method (Grunberg-Nissan at G = 0 / idealMixing) has no stated uncertainty, so nothing is counted
proposed_wording: 'A declared correlation names its constituent set and basis exactly as a solution record does (`system ( NaOH water ); basis analytical;`) and applies only to a phase whose present constituents are that set; a name in its formula that is not a constituent of the set is refused at compile time.'

case: tutorials/steady/optimisation/optim05_reactor_npv: SQP over variables.T_feed (348-352.5 K) of a CSTR whose inlet is the case feed (ethanol + acetic acid, both associating); the CSTR's residence time is F*sum z_i Vliq_i today (CSTR.cpp:245-251), a density in the pilot
what_the_rule_does: Any value that beats the catalogue (a measured point on the fed stream, or a declared correlation) prints both values per (method, site).  Under an outer driver the caveat block and divergence banner report ONE named pass (CLAUDE.md sec 6, 2026-09-07); the result JSON and goldens carry the chosen value only.  A point admitted 'at the declared state' (amendment 1) applies at iterates whose T_feed equals its T and not at the others
why_wrong_or_fine: WRONG.  (i) a deviation found at a pass that is not the reported one is lost to every surface but the console scroll; (ii) the objective NPV(T_feed) acquires a jump of the size of the deviation where the point stops applying, which an SQP differentiating by finite differences reads as a gradient -- a concrete case where the order shapes the answer with the deviation printed and nothing downstream showing it
proposed_wording: 'Under an outer driver a state-dependent choice (a point measurement) is decided ONCE on the base pass and frozen for every pass, announced; a pass whose state leaves the frozen choice's conditions refuses.  The LARGEST deviation of the run, with the state and pass it occurred at, is published in the result JSON (both values) and pinned by a golden row.'

case: optim05 again (no solution record for ethanol / water / acetic acid / ethyl acetate) or any molecular mixture
what_the_rule_does: Amendment 2 counts a finding 'when the deviation exceeds the stated uncertainty of the catalogue method'.  The beaten method there is idealMixing, whose evidence is 'not quantified unless measured' (sec 3.1 table); a composite has no stated uncertainty; bareRackett carries a generic 15 %
why_wrong_or_fine: WRONG for the commonest situation: a declared or measured value 30 % from ideal mixing can never be a counted finding, and one 14 % from a bare-Rackett leaf never either.  The danger the decline names (silence) returns in exactly the cases where the catalogue is weakest
proposed_wording: 'When the beaten method states no uncertainty, the deviation is compared with the expected error the method's registration declares from the literature (sec 2.1: Spencer-Danner about 7 %, Rackett 2 % / 15 %, ...); a method with neither counts every deviation above 1 %.'

case: (1) water: IF97 pure-fluid route (density() today, case-declared) and the IAPWS-95 Helmholtz record (referenceEoS) -- both tier 2b; (2) two measured files both at their conditions; (3) a case-local constant/parameters/solution record and the standards one; (4) Grunberg-Nissan at G = 0 and logMoleAverage, both tier 4 and numerically identical here (0.9348 mPa s); (5) the 24 case dicts that DECLARE `model BrockBird`
what_the_rule_does: sec 3.3 orders tiers but states no tie-breaker and does not say whether an explicit `model X;` already in a case is a pin or one candidate
why_wrong_or_fine: AMBIGUOUS.  (5) decides the migration: 9 of those cases carry water, whose record law gives 71.49 against Brock-Bird's 106.53 mN/m; if the declaration pins, the +49 % stays; if precedence applies, sigma moves -33 % in nine cases at S5
proposed_wording: 'Within a tier the case decides: an explicit method name in the case pins it (printed as chosen by the case); otherwise case-local before standards; two applicable items of the same kind (two measurements, two reference equations) REFUSE naming both until the case selects one.'

point: (b) point only on a fixed-state stream
case: The pilot itself (amendment 1): one stream, feed -> pump -> CSTR; a user's point on the fed stream (D3)
what_the_rule_does: The pump reads its inlet = the feed (fixed): the point applies.  The CSTR reads its inlet = the pump outlet, which is computed (P raised, T raised by the pump's heat), so the point is not admitted there and the CSTR gets the law
why_wrong_or_fine: WRONG.  One liquid, separated only by a pump's pressure rise, gets two densities -- the confusion amendment 5 defers local values to avoid.  The rule also names two kinds of stream (fixed / iterated) while the pump outlet is a third (computed, not iterated)
proposed_wording: 'A point applies to every stream of its constituent set whose state lies within its declared tolerances at the CONVERGED answer.  The run first resolves without it; where the answer lies within a point's conditions, it re-solves with the point frozen and checks the answer again (the approach-direction pattern, gibbs13); a point whose conditions the second answer leaves is refused, never toggled.'

case: D3: point declared in w[water] = 0.700 at 298.15 K, 101.325 kPa; the fed stream declared by componentMolarFlows in 0/<stream> (as every corpus feed is)
what_the_rule_does: With tolerances out of the pilot, 'at the declared state' is an equality test on floating-point T, P and a mass fraction computed from molar flows
why_wrong_or_fine: AMBIGUOUS.  The D3 PASS ('wins at its state') is then decided by round-off; the pilot needs at least a numerical tolerance, which is the concept amendment 1 removed
proposed_wording: 'In the pilot a point applies within a fixed numerical tolerance (relative 1e-9 on each declared variable), stated; physical tolerances remain out.'

point: (b) a stream not fixed by the case where a point is the right datum
case: Evaporator product liquor at a declared target concentration (a design specification fixes its composition; the stream is computed); a plant densitometer reads exactly that liquor
what_the_rule_does: Not admitted (computed stream) -> only a CHECK
why_wrong_or_fine: Debatable but the datum is right there: the specification makes the state as fixed as a feed.  The criterion that matters is whether the state can leave the point's conditions during the solve, not who wrote it
proposed_wording: Covered by the AT-b1 wording (decided at the converged answer).

case: pricedDensity::select (PricedDensity.H:24-31, storage tanks and sizing inventories): drops a component ONLY where its pure density is not finite (above Tc), state by state; record sec 4.3 S2: its callers become `neglectedIn`
what_the_rule_does: neglectedIn lists components and neglects them at every state
why_wrong_or_fine: WRONG either way: a static list drops CO2 (Tc 304 K) also at 20 C where it has a volume (numbers move); a conditional form is a switch by state at Tc, which sec 3.3 forbids.  The same question is open for `massWithoutVolume` on CO2 in idealMixing (sec 3.2): applied at 20 C too, or only where the leaf refuses (a method change at 304 K, D4's FAIL)
proposed_wording: 'A hypothesis applies at every state of the stream (never only where a leaf refuses); a case wanting the state-dependent form declares the datum (v_inf) instead.  The migration of pricedDensity lists, per case, the states where the static form changes a number.'

case: tutorials/batch/plant/apalutamide01_tablets: spray solution of API + HPMCAS in acetone, HPMCAS 3.75 wt %, MW declared NOMINAL 1000 kg/kmol (constant/components/hpmcas.dat); x_HPMCAS 2.3e-3 nominal, 1.3e-4 at 18 kg/mol
what_the_rule_does: `neglectedIn { viscosity { components (hpmcas); maxMoleFraction 1e-3; ... } }` refuses with the nominal MW and is admitted with a realistic one; the report then shows 'largest neglected mole fraction 1.3e-4'
why_wrong_or_fine: WRONG: the polymer is what makes that solution viscous; a mole-fraction bound on a component whose MW is bookkeeping measures the bookkeeping
proposed_wording: 'For viscosity, surface tension and conductivity the limit is a MASS fraction; a mole-fraction limit is refused for a component whose record declares its MW nominal or per repeat unit.'

case: NaOH-water pump: `massWithoutVolume { components (NaOH) }` and `neglectedIn { density { components (NaOH) } }` both declared
what_the_rule_does: Not stated which applies; the first keeps NaOH's mass, the second drops it
why_wrong_or_fine: AMBIGUOUS (one component, two incompatible hypotheses on one property).  Merge is algebraically clean: massWithoutVolume is neglectedIn applied to the liquid VOLUME (V = sum over the rest of n_i v_i, mass kept) where neglectedIn{density} drops both
proposed_wording: Either refuse two hypotheses on one (component, property), or merge: `neglectedIn { liquidVolume { ... } }` (mass kept) beside `neglectedIn { density { ... } }`; keep `massWithoutVolume` only as the printed name of the first if the owner prefers the pedagogy.

case: Liquids above saturation pressure (RO high-pressure pumps, 60-80 bar; a 500 bar water point in D1)
what_the_rule_does: Amendment 6 announces 'pressure not applied' once per method and site; no word authorises it
why_wrong_or_fine: FINE as a default for the Pareto set (about 0.3 % on water at 70 bar), provided it is listed in the run header beside the declared hypotheses; no third word needed.  The genuine third mechanism already exists: a measurement's tolerance wider than its uncertainty (sec 3.3) is a hypothesis outside the vocabulary
proposed_wording: 'The run header lists every concession the run makes -- the declared hypotheses, the accepted estimates, the default pressure neglect and every widened measurement tolerance -- in one table.'

case: CO2 dissolved in water, idealMixing without v_inf, 304.13 K
what_the_rule_does: sec 3.3: reaching a hard limit is a refusal at that state; sec 3.2 names it for CO2
why_wrong_or_fine: STATED for leaves, NOT stated in general: whether the composite's tier uses a hypothesis-supplied leaf (provenance word "assumed") and where 'assumed' sits in the weakest-leaf order; and that the weakest-leaf rule lets a 1e-6 trace with a bare-Rackett leaf demote an IAPWS-water phase to tier 4
proposed_wording: 'A composite refuses when any leaf it needs refuses; a hypothesis leaf counts as provenance word "assumed", ranked below estimated; a leaf below a declared trace fraction does not set the composite's tier.'

what_the_rule_does: 'dimensions are checked' -- of the terms; the rate-law precedent also checks the RESULT against the expected dimension (ExpressionRate.cpp:383-395)
why_wrong_or_fine: UNDER-SPECIFIED: the result must carry the property's dimension; `m[i]` needs a declared solvent; basis of w/x (analytical or speciated) is not stated for a declared method although sec 3.1 requires every method to declare it
proposed_wording: 'The formula's result is checked against the property's dimension; `m[i]` requires the record's `solvent`; the block declares `basis`.'

point: sizing refusal with outer drivers and the time-integrated binaries
case: A sweep over feed composition through x_ethanol = 0 (pair absent) and > 0; a batch fermentation where ethanol appears over time
what_the_rule_does: Poor-when tests 'a pair with no interaction parameter where a member is associating' 'for the system'
why_wrong_or_fine: AMBIGUOUS: present components (state-dependent: refusal mid-sweep or mid-integration) or declared components (assembly)?  The record never mentions outer drivers or choupoBatch / choupoCtrl / choupoSemiContinuous; ApproximationAuthorisation is re-read per pass (ApproximationAuthorisation.H:100-109), so 'resolved at assembly' is per pass
proposed_wording: 'Poor-when and every precedence decision read the DECLARED components of the package, at assembly, once per run (not per pass, not per instant).'

case: MEA, DEA, MDEA, TEA, ethylene / diethylene / triethylene glycol, NH3, phenol, cresols, H2O2 (43 of 95 name-suggestive records carry none of the three facts)
what_the_rule_does: Absence proves nothing; no `false` exists; poor-when fires only on the positive fact
why_wrong_or_fine: No disagreement found in the corpus (case-local copies are overlays, e.g. solvent03's ethanol.dat `overlayOf`).  The defect is the false negative: Brock-Bird +49 % on ethylene glycol, +60 % on TEA, and MEA falls back to Brock-Bird with no law -- the guard of sec 3.7 cannot fire for them
proposed_wording: 'Poor-when applies when association is positive OR UNKNOWN for a component whose formula carries O or N together with H; a curator lifts it with a sourced `associating none { source }` -- the one place a negative fact is needed.'

point: mass diffusivity in the same frame
what_the_rule_does: sec 3.1: 'for diffusivity, one solute IN one phase'; sec 3.8: Wilke-Chang 'calls the solvent's viscosity method and the solute's molar volume at Tb'
why_wrong_or_fine: The inputs are NOT a state of the phase: the solvent's PURE viscosity (ThermoPackage.cpp:2233-2234), not the phase's, and a pure-solute volume at Tb, a state outside the phase.  The engine reads solute.Vliq() (WilkeChang.cpp:45), i.e. 47.0 cm3/mol for CO2 (a 273 K liquid): D 1.684e-9 vs 1.925e-9 measured correlation (-12.5 %).  One field, two required reference states (density: its stated T; Wilke-Chang: Tb)
proposed_wording: 'A composite may ask for a PURE-component property at a reference state of its own (Wilke-Chang: the solute's liquid volume at Tb, the solvent's pure viscosity at T); such sub-requests are listed in its tree.  In a multicomponent liquid the solvent is the declared mixture rule's (Perkins-Geankoplis), never the first component.'

point: migration: a slice that moves no number
case: S0a validated by byte-identical results on the witnesses and the approximations cases
what_the_rule_does: No stream table prints a density (sec 1.3); routes no case exercises (6 records on the flat branch, 19 bare-Rackett, the IF97 density route, 32 Vliq with no stated temperature) cannot be seen by any golden; S0a's change of the per-process flags (ThermoPackage.cpp:2431) to per (method, site) changes the caveat block of the result JSON
why_wrong_or_fine: INSUFFICIENT: byte-identical goldens prove nothing about an unexercised route, and 'results' must exclude the advisory block or S0a cannot pass
proposed_wording: 'Before S0 a characterisation bench evaluates every property through every current route for every catalogue record at three temperatures and two pressures, recorded; after S0 it must be byte-identical.  "Results" means streams, KPIs and goldens; the advisory block is compared separately and its differences listed.'

point: migration: can the pilot's judgement fail?
what_the_rule_does: D2 PASS has no accuracy threshold; D4 is held to 'the record's stated evidence', written by the same slice; D3 holds the law to 0.04 % -- its fit residual on its own 156 points -- against another laboratory's set; amendment 6 measures cost with no threshold; no condition is named under which the structure is discarded
why_wrong_or_fine: D1 and D5 can fail; D2 and D4 cannot fail on accuracy; D3 can fail for inter-laboratory scatter, not the structure
proposed_wording: 'Fail conditions, any one: a unit outside the two needed an edit to keep its number; a demonstration needed a component name or a per-component branch in the selector; the resolved-methods table differs between two runs or two orderings of components; D2 deviation > the method's stated expected error; D3 deviation > the stated uncertainty of the INDEPENDENT dataset; cost above a number the owner writes before the pilot starts.'
